headline: 10y -17bp Thursday, Nasdaq -2.6%, SOX -6.7%, Brent $114, IG spreads widest since May 2025
stance: Treasuries and the yen caught Thursday's haven bid; gold and credit did not. Brent at $114 and a French rating decision tonight are the weekend risk.

news.head: Western Digital beat, guided above, sold on the call
news.body: Q2 guide above consensus. The call turned to higher costs and capex. Closed -6.4% Thursday, before the print, with the memory group.

news.head: CoreWeave -10% Thursday to its lowest since May 2025
news.body: Cost of insuring its debt jumped with the stock. The neocloud is the AI-debt stress gauge: equity and CDS moved together.

news.head: SpaceX -9.1% Thursday on lock-up expiry, +2.8% pre-market
news.body: Pre-market bid (~5:45am ET) on a report it wants 80,000 US cell sites, in talks with Crown Castle. A fourth carrier, financed by a stock still unlocking.

news.head: Moderna -17.6% Thursday on a leaked vaccine readout
news.body: Merck confirmed a data leak on the partnered melanoma vaccine. -2% pre-market (~5:45am ET).

implications: Bonds hedged stocks Thursday; the haven trade is back. Oil now reads as a growth hit, not an inflation hit. Long duration is the trade into the Oct 28 FOMC.
Credit is wider than at any point since the 2025 tariff shock. That recovery needed a policy pause; this one needs capex returns, with four tech giants reporting next week.

watch.head: US flash PMIs today; Michigan final 10:00
watch.body: Fed blackout to the Oct 28 FOMC: hike odds next week 7%, December ~80%. Flash PMIs in France, Germany and the eurozone all missed this morning.

watch.head: Moody's on France, after the European close
watch.body: A downgrade is widely expected. ECB decision Oct 29, with Bunds bid on the PMI misses. Euro specs at the 1st percentile going in.

watch.head: Earnings: American Express before the open
watch.body: Consensus EPS $4.50, revenue $20.1bn. Intel reports Oct 29. The question is still whether a beat sells.

watch.head: Iran: Aramco clears Dhahran HQ; IRGC: transits halted
watch.body: One dead at Dammam airport; Shaybah drone intercepted. IRGC says 4 tankers hit, 3 mined; Trump calls it fake. US-Israel strikes planned post-midterms.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Biggest 10y drop since March 2023 Thursday, on Treasury-futures short covering, with Brent +4%. Oil now trades as a growth hit. Dec hike odds ~80% from ~90%; Oct 28 FOMC 7%.
French 10y 5.04% (~4am ET) from 5.06% Thursday, a 2002 high. French selling eased overnight; Bunds bid as eurozone PMIs missed. Moody's rules tonight.
Brent $114.06, +0.8% (~5am ET), highest since May; WTI $100.61. Spot Basrah ~$10 under Dubai: futures price risk, barrels move. Gold under $4,000 overnight, no haven bid.
sections.positioning: COT, Oct 13: euro and sterling specs 1st percentile, Swiss franc 94th, fourth and ninth weeks. A French downgrade tonight hits the euro short and the franc long together.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: SOX -6.7% Thursday, Nasdaq's worst day since June. Futures flat (~5:45am ET): S&P -0.1%, Nasdaq 100 +0.2%, Dow -0.5%. Stoxx 600 -0.4% (~4am ET).
Asia reversed: Kospi closed +0.3% after -4.1% intraday; ChiNext +4.2% after -3.2%; Hang Seng +0.7%. Memory and optical names bid pre-market.
Dow +1.7% on the week, Nasdaq -0.5% (through Thursday). Rotation out of AI, not out of equities. S&P mid-range again; Wednesday's test of the 7,800 top failed.
sections.positioning: COT, Oct 13, unchanged: Russell 2000 specs 99th percentile, Nasdaq 100 97th, VIX shorts 6th. Thursday's -2.6% landed on that long-index, short-vol book; VIX stayed under 20.

single_name.note: Reformation: 2 insider-buy rules fired, filing dated Oct 9, new to the list today. Above its 200-day; days to cover 3.0. Long setup, score 4 of 5.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Global IG spreads widest since May 2025 at 129bp (~4am ET); Asia IG dollar spreads widest since July 2025. Credit did not follow the Treasury rally.
Asia credit at Friday's open: regional CDS +1.5bp to 78, China tech +3-5bp, Korea and India IG +3bp. Contagion runs through the AI supply chain.
Neocloud CDS wider Thursday as the stocks fell. Hike odds down 10 points and spreads still wider: lower yields are a growth scare, not relief for leveraged borrowers.
sections.positioning: Dealer HY inventory 28th percentile, unchanged. Thin dealer books into a global widening mean gappy marks, not orderly ones.
